patch.value:
## Context
pm has ~60 top-level commands. Growth pattern: each feature added a new top-level entry (8 list-* status variants, 4 history-* commands, extension+package+install+upgrade, start-task/pause-task/close-task, meet/event/remind). Agents pay for this in context tokens (help + contracts) and in wrong-command retries.

## Decision (proposed)
1. Noun-first grammar: ONE top-level command per domain noun; target ~15 nouns.
2. Verbs/facets become subcommands (pm history repair) or flags (pm list --status closed), never new top-level commands.
3. Projections (status/type/format) are flags.
4. Sugar (shortcuts, lifecycle aliases, calendar) = hidden aliases or package-owned commands.
5. Zero spelling removal: every current invocation keeps working via alias shims that emit a one-line migration hint (config-suppressible: ux.deprecation_hints=false).
6. Contract table is the single source of truth; tiered help, completions, MCP tool names, and docs are generated from it.

## Alternatives considered
- Status quo (flat surface): rejected — surface keeps growing linearly with features.
- Hard rename with removals: rejected — breaks agents/scripts; violates zero-feature-loss constraint.
- Separate porcelain/plumbing binaries: rejected — doubles distribution surface; contradicts single-CLI ergonomics.

## Consequences
+ Help fits one screen; contracts shrink; discoverability via noun help pages.
- Alias shim layer must be tested (spelling-parity spec) and carried for at least one deprecation cycle.
- Full wiring checklist per rename (commands/index, register-mutation, mcp/server, sdk/cli-contracts, contracts.ts, completions bash/zsh/fish, docs, vitest.config, contracts:update).
ADR: noun-verb CLI grammar — consolidation principles and alias-preserving deprecation policy (proposed)

Fixes the grammar rules for the CLI simplification epic pm-n7rr: noun-first top-level commands, verbs/facets as subcommands, projections as flags, sugar as hidden aliases, zero spelling removal, contracts as single source of truth for help/completions/MCP/docs. Status open = proposed; close = accepted. Duplicate check: no existing ADR covers command grammar.

ADR body records context, decision drivers, considered alternatives (flat surface status quo; git-style pure subcommands; busybox multi-binary), chosen grammar rules 1-6, and consequences incl. migration/deprecation policy; accepted (closed) before any pm-n7rr implementation task starts

value.author: maintainer-agent
value.text: Audit 2026-07-05 (second pass) surfaced two mapping conflicts the accepted ADR must fix: (1) restore is claimed by BOTH the history cluster (pm-tqel puts it under pm history subcommands) and the epic target surface (close/close-many/delete/restore) — pick one home; the bulk-lifecycle task pm-ik19 implements whichever placement is accepted. (2) eval is claimed by BOTH pm-6apl (ops cluster: stats/health/validate/gc/telemetry/eval) and the epic target surface (search (eval)) — pick one. Also: three clusters named in the target surface previously had no implementing child; now filed as pm-yql1 (item annotation facets), pm-ik19 (bulk/destructive lifecycle variants), pm-kcs4 (context/next/focus navigation noun).

value.author: claude-code-agent
value.text: Review response: resolved the two mapping conflicts recorded earlier for the proposed grammar. Restore belongs under the history noun because it replays audited history state; eval belongs under ops because it is a diagnostics/evaluation surface. pm-n7rr and pm-6apl were updated to match this target surface.

value.author: maintainer-agent
value.text: Audit #7 mapping addendum (proposed for acceptance with the ADR): (1) 'aggregate' joins the query-read noun as a pm list projection (e.g. pm list --aggregate <spec>) rather than a top-level command — it is a projection over the same filter surface, matching rule 3. (2) 'test-all' becomes an ops verb (pm ops test-all or pm ops test --all) since it is a workspace-wide diagnostic run, not an item facet; the per-item 'test' facet stays with the annotation-facet grammar (pm-yql1). (3) Package-owned top-level commands (beads, changelog) are explicitly OUT of the core noun budget — they already conform to rule 4 and register via the extension command surface. With these three, all 64 live top-level spellings (measured 2026-07-06) have exactly one home in the target grammar.

value.author: codex
value.text: Grammar audit addendum 2026-07-06/07 codex: the accepted grammar should explicitly classify internal/plumbing commands separately from core nouns and package-owned sugar. test-runs-worker is currently visible in default help/contracts despite being described as internal; pm-lp4j tracks hiding it from default discovery while preserving explicit internal orchestration access.

value.author: maintainer-agent
value.text: Brainstorm addition for the accepted revision (2026-07-07): add a principle 7 — SHARED VERB VOCABULARY. Every noun uses the same small verb set where the semantic exists: list / show / add / edit / remove / run / verify (+ noun-specific verbs only when unavoidable, e.g. history repair|redact|compact, plan materialize). Rationale: agents transfer knowledge across nouns without reading per-noun help (pm comments add == pm files add == pm schema add); wrong-verb retries drop the same way wrong-command retries do. Suggested test: a contracts-table lint asserting each noun's verbs are drawn from the shared vocabulary or an ADR-listed exception. Also suggest the ADR records a measurable acceptance target from the pm-a22j baseline (e.g. top-level help and contracts --summary each under a fixed token budget) so "simpler" is verifiable, not aesthetic.

value.author: maintainer-agent
value.text: Decision-support input 2026-07-11 (review pass): (1) Surface growth continues while proposed — top-level help now lists 64 entries (ADR context said ~60 on 07-06); contract table carries 105 commands + 86 actions. Every pass this stays open, the shim/parity work in pm-0z7n gets bigger. (2) NEW evidence the grammar must cover EXTENSION command synthesis: GH-503 (pm-s9iu) shows each extension group today spawns flattened top-level aliases (csv, csv-export, csv-import, jira, jira-sync all advertised in pm --help) and those aliases carry broken contracts (empty --help, no unknown-option validation). Recommend an explicit decision point: extensions contribute exactly ONE noun (the group); flattened <group>-<sub> aliases become hidden shims under point-5 policy or are not advertised in top-level help. That shrinks both the token surface and the GH-503 defect class at the design level. (3) Sequencing: points 1-4+6 are accept-able now — the only carried risk is the shim layer, and pm-0z7n already owns spelling-parity testing; this ADR gates pm-0z7n which gates 8 further items (tnud/tqel/pfqi/ik19/6apl/kcs4/yql1/o3fh/eq4x/0mox), the single largest decision bottleneck in the graph alongside pm-bl8x.

value.author: maintainer-agent
value.text: Decision-support input (pass evidence 2026-07-11, source GH-509/pm-fjxm): composed operations are a live grammar gap. GH-509 requests atomic select-and-claim and proposes the spelling `pm next --claim`, while main already ships `pm claim --next` (pm-114v). Two verbs each claiming the composition = exactly the surface-growth pattern this ADR exists to stop. Proposed rule for the ADR: (1) a composition lives on the MUTATING verb (claim), never the read verb (next) — reads stay side-effect-free so agents can poll them safely; (2) when a mutating verb embeds a selector, it reuses the read verb's filter contract verbatim (one shared candidate-selector flag set, defined once in cli-contracts), never a re-spelled subset. Consequence: GH-509 lands as claim --next + next's filters, and `next --claim` is rejected as a spelling. This also generalizes: any future `pm <read> --<mutate>` request should be flipped to `pm <mutate> --<selector>`.

value.author: codex-root
value.text: Decision support 2026-07-13: the current public root exposes 67 subcommands even though several are aliases, lifecycle variants, extension-owned audits, or an internal worker. The proposed noun-oriented grammar can reduce discovery burden without capability loss if compatibility aliases remain contract-visible, deprecation is measurable, extension ownership stays explicit, and JSON/TOON plus stdin/stdout composition remain first-class. Resolve this ADR before pm-0z7n and its downstream consolidation work; this audit records evidence only and does not accept the proposed decision.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Grammar input 2026-07-26: five core nouns need an ownership ruling under the noun-first principle — graph, merge, events, copy, normalize. graph is the substantive one: it is a 16-subcommand analytics and governance family, and the plausible readings are that it is its own domain noun, that its query verbs belong under a read noun while its audit and index verbs belong under ops, or that it is the read surface of the relationship facet already enumerated under item facets. merge and events are single-verb surfaces that plausibly fold under history or ops. copy is a create variant. normalize is a governance verb that already exists as a package capability. The earlier ruling pattern on this ADR — restore under history because it replays audited state, eval under ops because it is diagnostic — is the precedent to apply.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Decision-forcing evidence, measured 2026-07-27: the surface this ADR proposes to consolidate is growing faster than the ADR is being decided.

Top-level spelling count taken from the shipped build at each census recorded on pm-n7rr, plus today's:

  2026-07-05  ~60   (the count this ADR was written against)
  2026-07-06   64
  2026-07-07   65
  2026-07-18   73
  2026-07-25   77
  2026-07-26   88
  2026-07-27   89

That is +29 spellings in 22 days, roughly +1.3 per day, or +48 percent against the number in the ADR text. The proposal itself has not changed and is not the bottleneck; the twelve-noun table, the shared verb vocabulary and the placement disposition for the five previously unplaced nouns are all recorded on pm-n7rr as notes 8, 11 and 13, and every option there is alias-preserving with zero feature loss.

Two consequences follow for whoever decides this.

First, the cost of deferral is not zero and is not constant. Every new top-level spelling added while the ADR sits open is another alias the shim layer must carry forever under the alias-preserving policy this ADR itself mandates. Deferral does not preserve optionality here, it spends it: the migration gets strictly larger and the eventual v1.0 grammar freeze on pm-xp1xsw freezes a larger surface.

Second, an interim control is available that does not require deciding the ADR. Accepting or rejecting the noun table is a design judgment; refusing to let the count grow while that judgment is pending is not. That control has been recorded as an acceptance criterion on pm-wt43zj so it can ship independently of this decision, and it should be read as reducing the pressure on this ADR rather than pre-empting it.

Nothing here argues for a particular disposition of the noun table. It argues that the option being exercised by not deciding — a surface that keeps growing under an alias-preservation promise — is the one option nobody chose.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Complete placement table, recorded 2026-07-28. This is the artifact the ADR has been missing: every rendered top-level spelling mapped to exactly one target noun-verb path, so acceptance is a ruling on a table rather than on a principle. It supersedes nothing and renumbers nothing; the four earlier decision-support notes stay as recorded. Live census at HEAD: 85 rendered top-level spellings, 70 contracted command summaries.

TWELVE NOUNS. item, list, context, search, graph, history, workspace, package, ops, plan, contracts, help.

The tension this table resolves. Noun-first consolidation is right for legibility and wrong for the hot path: an agent that runs create, get, update, close, claim, release hundreds of times per session should not pay two tokens where one suffices, and the recorded op histogram says thirteen operations are 99.4 percent of all mutations with the annotation family alone at 46.7 percent. So the rule proposed here is asymmetric on purpose. Canonical form is always noun-verb. A named set of fourteen bare-verb spellings on the hottest paths are PERMANENT aliases, declared as such in contract data, exempt from deprecation and counted separately from the legacy hidden aliases that exist only for compatibility. Everything else consolidates.

NOUN 1 - item. The unit of work, its lifecycle, and its facets.
  create           -> item create              permanent bare alias
  copy             -> item create --from       hidden alias
  get              -> item get                 permanent bare alias
  update           -> item update              permanent bare alias
  update-many      -> item update --many       hidden alias
  close            -> item close               permanent bare alias
  close-many       -> item close --many        hidden alias
  delete           -> item delete              permanent bare alias
  restore          -> item restore             permanent bare alias, see open ruling A
  claim            -> item claim               permanent bare alias
  release          -> item release             permanent bare alias
  append           -> item append              hidden alias
  start-task       -> item claim --start       hidden alias
  pause-task       -> item release --pause     hidden alias
  close-task       -> item close               hidden alias
  comments         -> item comments            permanent bare alias
  notes            -> item notes               permanent bare alias
  learnings        -> item learnings           permanent bare alias
  files            -> item files               permanent bare alias
  docs             -> item docs                permanent bare alias
  deps             -> item deps                permanent bare alias, see open ruling D
  test             -> item test                see open ruling B
  item             -> the noun itself, already rendered
  meet, event, remind -> calendar package create sugar, leaves core, owned by pm-o3fh

NOUN 2 - list. Everything that returns rows selected by predicate.
  list             -> list
  list-all, list-draft, list-open, list-in-progress, list-blocked, list-closed, list-canceled
                   -> list --status <s>        seven hidden aliases, owned by pm-pfqi
  aggregate        -> list --group-by          hidden alias, owned by pm-xkgq

NOUN 3 - context. The working set and what to do next.
  context, ctx     -> context
  next             -> context next             permanent bare alias, owned by pm-kcs4
  focus            -> context focus            hidden alias, owned by pm-kcs4

NOUN 4 - search. Retrieval by content.
  search           -> search
  search-advanced  -> package-contributed, renders under its owning package, see open ruling C

NOUN 5 - graph. Workspace-scoped traversal and analytics over typed edges. Promoted to a canonical noun per the 2026-07-26 placement note.
  graph            -> graph

NOUN 6 - history. The immutable record and its maintenance.
  history          -> history
  events           -> history events
  activity         -> history activity
  history-redact   -> history redact
  history-repair   -> history repair
  history-compact  -> history compact
  history-author-acknowledge -> history author-acknowledge
  All four history-* consolidations are owned by pm-tqel.

NOUN 7 - workspace. The tracker as an object: how it is created, configured, shaped, snapshotted, and reconciled across branches.
  init             -> workspace init           permanent bare alias
  config           -> workspace config         permanent bare alias
  schema           -> workspace schema
  profile          -> workspace profile
  templates        -> workspace templates      package-contributed
  merge            -> workspace merge          machine-facing git integration, absent from the agent-facing table
  workspace        -> the noun itself, already rendered, see open ruling E

NOUN 8 - package. Extensibility lifecycle. Owned by pm-tnud.
  package, packages -> package
  extension        -> package                  hidden alias
  install          -> package install          hidden alias
  upgrade          -> package upgrade          hidden alias

NOUN 9 - ops. Diagnostics and maintenance that act on the workspace rather than an item. Owned by pm-6apl.
  stats            -> ops stats
  health           -> ops health
  validate         -> ops validate
  gc               -> ops gc
  telemetry        -> ops telemetry
  eval             -> ops eval
  normalize        -> ops normalize            placement resolved here per the 2026-07-26 note, with the validate --auto-fix overlap dispositioned at the same time
  reindex          -> ops reindex
  duplicates       -> ops duplicates
  test-all         -> ops test                 see open ruling B

NOUN 10 - plan. Durable multi-step planning.
  plan             -> plan

NOUN 11 - contracts. The machine-readable surface description. Stays a top-level noun because it is the bootstrap path every other surface is discovered through, and burying it under help would make discovery depend on the human surface.
  contracts        -> contracts

NOUN 12 - help. The human twin of contracts.
  help             -> help
  pm               -> declared exempt self-name, see pm-1jrdri

PACKAGE-CONTRIBUTED SPELLINGS. Sixteen of the eighty-five come from packages and render identically to core commands, which is the single largest legibility problem in the current surface and is not solved by any noun placement: beads, cal, calendar, changelog, command-kit, comments-audit, dedupe-audit, dedupe-merge, duplicates, eval, normalize, reindex, search-advanced, templates, test-runs, todos, twin, vcs. An agent cannot tell from help which of these exist in a bare install, and pm-n7rr already records that they exit 2 when the owning package is absent. The table above places each by function, but the ADR must also rule on whether package-contributed commands render in a distinct section, under a package-qualified path, or with a declared owner field that help renders.

FIVE OPEN RULINGS the ADR must settle to be acceptable.

Ruling A - restore. This table places restore under item because it restores one item to one version. pm-tqel proposes folding restore under history alongside redact, repair and compact. Both readings are defensible: the mechanism is a history replay, the subject is an item. Proposed resolution: item restore is canonical because the noun is the subject not the mechanism, and history keeps stream-level maintenance only. This also keeps the pm-34w8za consolidation coherent, since that item groups redact, repair and compact as stream maintenance and explicitly reaches into restore only as a clone source.

Ruling B - test has three scopes and one spelling. item test manages and runs the linked tests of one item. ops test runs everything. test-runs inspects the package-owned background runner. Proposed resolution: item test and ops test as above, test-runs stays package-contributed, and the internal test-runs-worker entrypoint is hidden per pm-lp4j.

Ruling C - package-contributed rendering, as described above.

Ruling D - deps versus graph. Both read the same typed edges. Proposed resolution: item deps is the item-scoped, budget-bounded relationship view an agent uses inside a task; graph is the workspace-scoped analytic surface. They are different questions over one substrate and both keep their names, with the boundary declared in contract data so neither grows into the other.

Ruling E - the workspace noun is already occupied and uncontracted. workspace renders in help today and exits 2 on pm contracts --command workspace, filed as pm-1jrdri. Adopting workspace as a canonical noun means that defect must be fixed first, otherwise the grammar's own noun is the one command the contract system cannot describe.

WHAT THIS TABLE DOES NOT DO. It removes nothing. Every one of the eighty-five spellings resolves after consolidation, fourteen as permanent bare aliases and the remainder as hidden compatibility aliases counted by pm-0mox. It does not renumber or supersede the existing consolidation tasks under pm-n7rr; each task keeps its scope and gains a target path from this table. And it does not decide the flag lexicon: pm-fs8q9x must land first, because folding the seven list-* variants into list --status is a null move for token cost if the flag spelling per concept is still ambiguous.

author: harness:claude-code
message: Ruling E: adopting workspace as a canonical noun requires the uncontracted workspace command to be fixed first

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Ruling F, proposed 2026-07-29: the unit of consolidation is the flag concept, not the command noun, and the noun table is the second tranche rather than the first.

The measurement that forces it. The live surface is 84 commands, 1,792 flag occurrences and 481 distinct flag spellings. Two hundred spellings appear on exactly one command. The eight list-family commands carry 63 to 65 flags each and differ in one status literal. Create, update and update-many together spend 288 occurrences, sixteen percent of the whole surface, re-declaring one item schema three times.

What the noun table does and does not buy. Collapsing 85 spellings to 12 nouns with 14 permanent bare-verb aliases makes the index legible and makes the product describable in one screen, which is worth doing and stays the target shape. It removes zero flag spellings. An agent that has learned the twelve nouns still cannot predict whether a filter it used on list works on aggregate, still cannot predict whether an acceptance criterion is set with --ac or --add-ac, and still faces 200 spellings it can only learn by reading one command's help. The noun table changes what the agent reads first; the flag lexicon changes how much it has to remember.

The ruling. Sequence the program as flag-lexicon first, nouns second. Concretely: a declared filter predicate consumed by every query surface, a declared item field set consumed by every mutation verb, and a declared disposition of local or shared on every one of the 200 singleton spellings. Only then re-render the nouns, because at that point the noun table is a presentation change over a governed vocabulary rather than a rename over an ungoverned one.

Consequence for rulings A through E. None of them is invalidated, but three change character. Ruling B, the three scopes of test, is a field-set question once the field set is declared, because the scopes differ in which declared fields apply rather than in which verb is spelled. Ruling D, deps versus graph, is a predicate question once the predicate is declared, because the two commands differ in traversal semantics and not in filtering. Ruling C, the sixteen package-contributed spellings, becomes tractable only after the singleton disposition exists, because a package flag is by definition a singleton and today nothing distinguishes a package flag from a core one in the rendered surface. Rulings A and E are unaffected.

Falsifiable prediction attached to this ruling. If the noun consolidation lands before the flag work, the count of distinct flag spellings will not fall and the per-command help total will not fall by more than the removed index rows, roughly 3 percent of 212,496 bytes. That is checkable after the fact and should be checked, because if it turns out false this ruling was wrong.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Placement input for the seven spellings that landed after the noun table (workspace, eval, item, duplicates, start-task, pause-task, close-task) plus a three-pattern classification of the residual redundancy and a fourth metric - distinct spelling-and-concept pairs rather than flag count - are recorded as a note on pm-n7rr dated 2026-07-29. The table, the fourteen bare-verb aliases and the five open rulings are unchanged; ruling C on package-contributed spellings and the new ruling this raises on whether item or the bare verbs are canonical are the two that gate the fold.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Ruling F (open) — one flag name carries exactly one value domain across the whole surface, and a paired flag shares one value grammar with its partner

Two live violations force this ruling rather than leaving it implicit in the noun table.

First, --for. It resolves a declared read intent on get, list, next and search, and it is validated against the context section enum on context. The intent applier assigns a contract's included_field_groups array straight into the section option, and four of the five groups in one declared intent are not section names, so both context intents are unreachable and the resulting error names --section, a flag the caller never passed. The grammar question this raises is not a bug report: it is whether a flag name is allowed to mean different things on different nouns at all. Ruling: no. A flag name is a surface-wide term. If two commands need different domains, they need different flag names, or one contract-declared mapping between the domains that is itself testable.

Second, --dep and --dep-remove. The add half refuses the unprefixed comma form with an explicit message naming both accepted shapes. The remove half accepts it, matches nothing, and exits 0 reporting zero changed fields. Ruling: a mutating flag pair over one concept declares one value grammar, and both halves validate against it. A remove that matches nothing is a diagnosable outcome, not success.

Consequence for the twelve-noun table. Both rulings are preconditions for the table being writable as data rather than prose. A noun table that fixes command names while flag names remain per-command terms has not fixed the grammar - it has only fixed the first token. Ruling F therefore belongs in the same ADR as the noun placement and should be settled before the consolidation slices begin, because every slice that moves a spelling also moves its flags.

Relationship to the existing open rulings. A (restore placement), B (test's three scopes), C (the 16 package-contributed spellings) and D (deps versus graph) all decide where a capability lives. E decides whether an uncontracted noun may render. F is the first ruling about the token after the noun, which is why it does not collapse into any of them.
